ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the length of line segment $AC=12\, \text{cm}$, and point $B$ is on line segment $AC$, satisfying $BC= \frac{1}{2} AB$. If $D$ is the midpoint of $AB$, and $E$ is the midpoint of $AC$, find the length of $DE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $D$ is the midpoint of $AB$,\\
thus $AD=\frac{1}{2}AB=4\text{cm}$,\\
Since $E$ is the midpoint of $AC$,\\
thus $AE=\frac{1}{2}AC=6\text{cm}$,\\
Therefore, $DE=AE-AD=\boxed{2\text{cm}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a horizontal line segment, with five collinear points marked, in order from left to right as A, D, E, B, C; D is between A and B, E is between D and B, and B is between E and C. Therefore it can be handled according to the order A-D-E-B-C on the same straight line. Then reason: Let AB = x. Because B is on AC, and BC = 1/2 AB, so BC = x/2. Also AC = AB + BC = 12, so x + x/2 = 12, that is 3x/2 = 12, solving gives x = 8, therefore AB = 8 cm. D is the midpoint of AB, so AD = 1/2 AB = 4 cm. E is the midpoint of AC, so AE = 1/2 AC = 6 cm. From the figure, D is on the left side of E and both are on AC, DE = AE - AD = 6 - 4 = 2 cm.
